name: Asylum and Subsidiary Protection

qualifying_event.description: Asylum requires a well-founded fear of persecution owing to race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group, or political opinion. Subsidiary protection applies where asylum criteria aren't met but there are justified reasons to believe the person would face a real risk of serious harm (death penalty, torture, or serious threat from armed conflict) if returned to their country of origin.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Evidence supporting the persecution or serious-harm claim.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires meeting the criteria for asylum (well-founded fear of persecution) or subsidiary protection (real risk of serious harm if returned), assessed by the competent authority.

outcome.duration_length: asylum: residence permit valid 5 years; subsidiary protection: residence permit valid 3 years

sources.title: Ministarstvo unutarnjih poslova Republike Hrvatske (mup.gov.hr) -- Asylum and subsidiary protection

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Croatia's initial build. Unlike Barbados' bb_asylum (a 'never existed' closed case), Croatia has a real, EU Common European Asylum System-compliant domestic protection framework, confirmed at tier-1. Asylees get immediate work authorisation without a separate permit and up to 2 years of state-funded accommodation; both are real entitlements, not modelled as separate schema fields. work_rights set to 'full' (not 'restricted') per the source's explicit 'immediate employment authorization without additional permits' -- a notable, confirmed difference from Estonia's international-protection route, where work rights were left 'restricted' for lack of a clear source statement. pr_after_months (60) reflects protection-holders' residence feeding hr_long_term_residence's or hr_permanent_stay's own tests (both allow asylum/subsidiary-protection time to count, per those routes' sourcing), not a separate stated figure for this route specifically. Obligations include registering residence within 15 days and attending Croatian language/history/culture courses -- procedural, not modelled as qualifying requirements.
